title: Flat module lifts and bounded-above derived lifts
statement:
Let $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjection of commutative rings with nilpotent kernel $I$, meaning $I^r=0$ for some integer $r\ge1$. Let $A'\to P'$ be a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], set $P=P'\otimes_{A'}A$, and let $M$ be a $P$-module flat over $A$. Use ordinary tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], the module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived tensor computed by total tensor of K-flat resolutions [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Write $M[0]$ for the module in degree zero and $D^-(P')$ for the objects whose cohomology vanishes in sufficiently large degrees. The following are equivalent: (i) there is a $P'$-module $L$, flat over $A'$, with a $P$-linear isomorphism $L\otimes_{A'}A\cong M$; (ii) there is $C'\in D^-(P')$ with an isomorphism $C'\otimes_{P'}^{\mathbf L}P\cong M[0]$. Furthermore, if $I^2=0$ and $J=IP'\subset P'$ (an ordinary $P$-module because $J^2=0$), flatness identifies $J\cong I\otimes_A P$ and the canonical derived-to-ordinary tensor map is an isomorphism in $D(P)$:
$$M[0]\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}J[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}(M\otimes_PJ)[0]\cong(M\otimes_A I)[0].$$
No finite generation or Noetherian hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Assume (i) and put $C'=L[0]$. Apply flat-algebra derived tensor exchange with $(R,S,N,K)=(A',P',A,L[0])$. A free resolution $F^\bullet\to A[0]$ over $A'$ becomes, after tensoring with the $A'$-flat module $L$, an augmented complex exact away from degree zero, by flat tensor exactness. Its zeroth cohomology is $L\otimes_{A'}A=M$. The augmentation compatibility of the exchange identifies the resulting isomorphism with the canonical map $L[0]\otimes_{P'}^{\mathbf L}P\to(L\otimes_{P'}P)[0]$. This is a $P$-linear isomorphism: forgetting to $P'$ does not change kernels, images or cohomology. The balancing maps $l\otimes(p'\otimes a)\mapsto p'l\otimes a$ and $l\otimes a\mapsto l\otimes(1\otimes a)$ identify the ordinary target with $M[0]$. Thus (ii) holds.

source.place: Tag 0DZ1, lemma-lift-equivalence-module-derived, proof; typed tensor directions and low-degree edge corrected as recorded in report.md.

proof.text: Record the elementary top-degree calculation used below. If $B$ is a commutative ring, $E\in D(B)^{\le t}$ and $V$ is a $B$-module, tensor the successive-truncation triangle $U=\tau_{\le t-1}E\to E\to H^t(E)[-t]\to U[1]$ with $V[0]$. Derived tensor is triangulated; the upper-bound lemma puts $U\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}V[0]$ in degrees at most $t-1$. Its cohomology in degrees $t,t+1$ is zero, so the cohomology exact sequence gives $H^t(E\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}V[0])\cong H^t(E)\otimes_B V$; the last identification is the degree-zero derived-module Tor comparison. The same upper-bound lemma gives $E\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}V[0]\in D(B)^{\le t}$. These conclusions use no finiteness or lower bound.

source.place: Tag 0DZ1, lemma-lift-equivalence-module-derived, proof; typed tensor directions and low-degree edge corrected as recorded in report.md.

proof.text: Now assume (ii). By tensor right exactness applied to $I\to A'\to A\to0$, the map $P'\to P$ is surjective with kernel $J=IP'$. Since $J^r=I^rP'=0$, any $P'$-module $T$ with $T\otimes_{P'}P=0$ satisfies $T=JT=J^2T=\cdots=J^rT=0$; no finite-generation version of Nakayama is being used. If $C'$ had nonzero positive cohomology, bounded-aboveness would give a largest such degree $t>0$. Step 2 gives $H^t(C')\otimes_{P'}P=H^t(M[0])=0$, contrary to this nilpotent argument. Hence $C'\in D(P')^{\le0}$. This also covers $M=0$ without choosing a largest degree of a zero complex.

source.place: Tag 0DZ1, lemma-lift-equivalence-module-derived, proof; typed tensor directions and low-degree edge corrected as recorded in report.md.

proof.text:
Set $L=H^0(C')$. Step 2 with $t=0$ gives $L\otimes_{P'}P\cong M$, hence also $L\otimes_{A'}A\cong M$ by the balancing maps of step 1. Tensor the triangle $U=\tau_{\le-1}C'\to C'\to L[0]\to U[1]$ with $P$. Here $U\otimes_{P'}^{\mathbf L}P$ has cohomology only in degrees at most $-1$. Its degree-zero vanishing and the cohomology exact sequence give a SURJECTION
$$H^{-1}(C'\otimes_{P'}^{\mathbf L}P)\twoheadrightarrow H^{-1}(L[0]\otimes_{P'}^{\mathbf L}P)=\operatorname{Tor}^{P'}_1(L,P).$$
The source is $H^{-1}(M[0])=0$, so this Tor module is zero. This is the required low-degree edge argument; it does not assume $C'$ is already a module, or infer anything about all its negative cohomology.

source.place: Tag 0DZ1, lemma-lift-equivalence-module-derived, proof; typed tensor directions and low-degree edge corrected as recorded in report.md.

proof.text: Apply flat-algebra derived tensor exchange once more, now with $(R,S,N,K)=(A',P',A,L[0])$. Forgetting to $A'$ and taking degree $-1$ identifies the zero Tor module of step 4 with $\operatorname{Tor}^{A'}_1(L,A)$; use the derived-module Tor comparison on both sides. Tor symmetry gives $\operatorname{Tor}^{A'}_1(A,L)=0$. The first-variable Tor exact sequence for $0\to I\to A'\to A\to0$ therefore makes $I\otimes_{A'}L\to A'\otimes_{A'}L=L$ injective. This is multiplication. Also $L/IL\cong L\otimes_{A'}A\cong M$ (the quotient map and inverse send $l\otimes\bar a$ to $al\bmod IL$ and $l\bmod IL$ to $l\otimes1$), so it is $A$-flat. The cited nilpotent-ideal module flatness theorem applies with $R=A'$, ideal $I$, exponent $r$, and module $L$, and gives $A'$-flatness. This proves (i).

source.place: Tag 0DZ1, lemma-lift-equivalence-module-derived, proof; typed tensor directions and low-degree edge corrected as recorded in report.md.

proof.text: For the last assertion suppose $I^2=0$. Tensor $0\to I\to A'\to A\to0$ with the $A'$-flat module $P'$. Flat tensor exactness gives $I\otimes_{A'}P'\cong J$. The elements of $I$ are annihilated by $I$ and those of $J$ by $J$. Balancing thus gives $I\otimes_{A'}P'\cong I\otimes_A P$: send $i\otimes p'$ to $i\otimes\bar p'$; a lift of $\bar p'$ defines the inverse since changing the lift by $\sum a_kp'_k$, $a_k\in I$, changes the tensor by $\sum a_ki\otimes p'_k=0$. Moreover $P$ is $A$-flat: for an injection of $A$-modules $V\to W$, the identification $V\otimes_A P=V\otimes_{A'}P'$ (and the same for $W$) reduces injectivity to $A'$-flatness of $P'$.

source.place: Tag 0DZ2, lemma-lift-equivalence-module, square-zero paragraph and explicit free-A-resolution footnote; Tag 0DZ1 for the preceding equivalence.

proof.text: Apply the new tensor exchange with $(R,S,N,K)=(A,P,I,M[0])$, justified by step 6. It identifies $M[0]\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}(P\otimes_A I)[0]$ in $D(P)$ with $Q_P(M\otimes_A F^\bullet)$ for a free $A$-resolution $F^\bullet\to I[0]$. Flat tensor exactness for the $A$-flat module $M$ says its augmentation to $(M\otimes_A I)[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. By the augmentation clause of the exchange, this augmentation is precisely the canonical derived-to-ordinary comparison followed by balancing. Substitute the $P$-linear identification $J\cong P\otimes_A I$ of step 6. The balancing map $m\otimes(p\otimes i)\mapsto pm\otimes i$, with inverse $m\otimes i\mapsto m\otimes(1\otimes i)$, gives $M\otimes_PJ\cong M\otimes_A I$. Thus the specified canonical comparison is an isomorphism in $D(P)$, not merely an equality of its cohomology groups.
